newsitem.title: USA: NAR's Tucillo sees US housing market leveling off.
newsitem.headline: NAR's Tucillo sees US housing market leveling off.

text.p: The U.S. housing market has been helped recently by mild weather and anticipation of an interest-rate rise by the Federal Reserve but it should level off soon, John Tucillo, chief economist for the National Association of Realtors, said Thursday.
"The housing market will be down over the next few months," Tucillo told a news conference.

Just prior to the news conference, the NAR reported that sales of existing U.S. homes rose 9.0 percent in February to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.26 million units. The February sales rate was the second highest on record.
Looking at the factors affecting the February home sales, Tucillo said low rates and the expectation that they would increase most certainly played a role.
"At about the time these sales were being committed to, we began to see speculation about the Fed's rate increase," Tucillo said.
"Very clearly, we have had a very, very mild weather in both the Northeast and MidWest and that has helped both home building and home sales," he added.
The Federal Reserve on Tuesday raised the key federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 percent.
Tucillo predicted "a very mild effect" on future home sales from the rate rise, in part because the increase was small and also because "interest rates are not particularly high."
